result.title: Expert-Guided Rubrics as Dense Reward Signals for Reinforcement Learning in Non-Verifiable Domains
result.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, RL4LLM-Agents workshop ICAIF ACM
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in non-verifiable domains such as financial services, where they must interpret user intent, rewrite queries, and retrieve information under domain-specific constraints. Although reinforcement learning (RL) can train such agents from the consequences of their actions, recent successes largely rely on verifiable tasks with automatically computed binary rewards. In non-verifiable retrieval tasks, assessing query quality requires scarce subject-matter expert (SME) judgment that is inherently graded rather than binary. With Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), sparse rewards yield no useful learning signal when all sampled outputs within a group receive the same outcome, causing optimization to stall. We introduce a method that converts a small, fixed investment of SME judgment into a dense reward and combines it with retrieval-based metrics to form a hybrid, GRPO-compatible training signal. Experiments show improvements of up to 6\% in Recall@3 and 6.7\% in MRR@3 compared with sparse-reward baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究非可验证领域（如金融服务查询改写与检索）中 LLM agent 的强化学习训练，把少量专家评分固化为稠密奖励，并与检索指标组合成 GRPO 可用的混合奖励信号，在 Recall@3 与 MRR@3 上优于稀疏奖励基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将稀疏专家判断转为稠密、分组可用的奖励设计，可能为 LVR 轨迹训练中的贡献分配与中间状态监督提供线索，但任务为纯文本检索、无视觉或 latent 状态，需核查可迁移性。
